headline: Trump thanks PM Tarique Rahman for billions in Boeing aircraft purchase
summary: US President Donald Trump expressed confidence in Bangladesh's bright future under PM Tarique Rahman's leadership and praised the aircraft deal.
details: US President Donald Trump sent a letter to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, expressing his hope to meet the PM soon and expressing confidence that Bangladesh and its people have a very bright future under his leadership.
In the letter, Trump thanked the Prime Minister for the decision to purchase Boeing aircraft, stating, "Boeing will not let you down, and I will not forget."

US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor recently stated that Bangladesh has committed billions of dollars to buy additional Boeing aircraft under a new deal between Dhaka and Washington.
In April, Bangladesh signed a deal with Boeing to buy 14 planes for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, a deal valued at $3.7 billion.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that the purchase is demand-driven and not due to US pressure, stating that Bangladesh needs to expand its fleet to open new routes and become an aviation hub in Asia.
Kobir mentioned that the growth of Ethiopian Airlines as an example of how fleet expansion can support the development of an international aviation network.
caption:
President Trump says "Boeing will not let you down" as Bangladesh commits billions to expand its aircraft fleet.

US President Donald Trump sent a letter to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, expressing his hope to meet the PM soon and expressing confidence that Bangladesh and its people have a very bright future under his leadership.

In the letter, Trump thanked the Prime Minister for the decision to purchase Boeing aircraft, stating, "Boeing will not let you down, and I will not forget."

US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor recently stated that Bangladesh has committed billions of dollars to buy additional Boeing aircraft under a new deal between Dhaka and Washington.

In April, Bangladesh signed a deal with Boeing to buy 14 planes for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, a deal valued at $3.7 billion.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that the purchase is demand-driven and not due to US pressure, stating that Bangladesh needs to expand its fleet to open new routes and become an aviation hub in Asia.

Kobir mentioned that the growth of Ethiopian Airlines as an example of how fleet expansion can support the development of an international aviation network.

headline_marked: 5 killed, including child, as [[US military strikes Iran]]
headline: 5 killed, including child, as US military strikes Iran
summary: The US military targeted IRGC sites, including air defense and radar systems, while Iran retaliated by attacking US assets in Jordan, Bahrain, and Iraq.
details: The US military has completed a wave of strikes on Iran, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) sites. The targets included air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, and communications sites.

According to the Iranian Red Crescent, five people were killed and 50 wounded at a wedding near Sirik, a coastal area on the Strait of Hormuz, during the strikes. A 4-year-old child was among the dead.
Iran retaliated on Tuesday by striking US assets in Jordan, Bahrain, and Iraq. This exchange marks the most serious escalation in weeks, contributing to a rise in global energy prices.

The conflict has seen further escalation with attacks on tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has effectively closed to shipping. An Axios report cited US officials stating that two Iranian government tankers were also attacked.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright noted that 17 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, the highest level since the war began reducing flows.
President Donald Trump stated on Tuesday that he was not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table and questioned when the Iranian people would rise up against their government.
caption:
A 4-year-old child is among 5 killed in a US military strike on a wedding in Iran.

The US military has completed a wave of strikes on Iran, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) sites. The targets included air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, and communications sites.

According to the Iranian Red Crescent, five people were killed and 50 wounded at a wedding near Sirik, a coastal area on the Strait of Hormuz, during the strikes. A 4-year-old child was among the dead.

Iran retaliated on Tuesday by striking US assets in Jordan, Bahrain, and Iraq. This exchange marks the most serious escalation in weeks, contributing to a rise in global energy prices.

The conflict has seen further escalation with attacks on tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has effectively closed to shipping. An Axios report cited US officials stating that two Iranian government tankers were also attacked.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright noted that 17 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, the highest level since the war began reducing flows.

President Donald Trump stated on Tuesday that he was not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table and questioned when the Iranian people would rise up against their government.
